title: Classifier Scenario Builder
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Concept Classifier Type
Sorting Quiz
Category Bucket
Builder MicroSim
Item Writing
description: A form for one concept-classifier scenario (scenario, correctAnswer, three distractors, hint, explanation) beside a live learner preview of the quiz card, with quality checks, a data.json export and a playable Try as learner mode.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: Writing a concept-classifier scenario with exactly one defensible option
learningObjectives: The learner will write a classifier scenario, four options, a hint and an explanation, and will check that exactly one option is defensible.
prerequisites: Concept Classifiers and Sorting Quizzes section of Chapter 11
The poster anti-patterns listed in Chapter 11

accessibility.notes: The form uses native text inputs and text areas; the JSON is a selectable read-only text area

controls.label: scenario, correctAnswer, three distractors, hint, explanation
controls.purpose: Author the scenario; the preview updates on every keystroke

controls.label: Check quality
controls.purpose: Flag empty fields, a missing or repeated correct answer, an over-long option and a hint that repeats the answer

controls.label: Show JSON / Hide JSON
controls.purpose: Display the scenario in the classifier data.json shape

controls.label: Try as learner / Back to editing
controls.purpose: Play the card with hint and feedback

controls.label: Start from
controls.purpose: Load the chapter example, a flawed draft or a blank form

controls.label: Only one option is defensible (I checked)
controls.purpose: Record the author's judgment that no distractor can be defended

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Builder with live preview, automatic string checks and a human-judgment check
keyQuestions: What makes a distractor plausible but indefensible?
Why do test-wise learners pick the longest option?
How can a hint help without naming the answer?
commonMisconceptions: Passing the automatic checks proves the item is good
A distractor should be obviously wrong
The hint may restate the category name
assessmentOpportunities: Scenarios that pass every automatic check
Peer attempts to defend each distractor
Exported JSON with all six fields
